raw_response:
I am getting old now, and I do things the way that keeps the family steady, not chasing fancy ideas. On my 18 mu, I will still keep most land in wheat-maize because that is the safe road here. Wheat gives us a steady harvest, maize follows right after, and if one side is not so good, the other can still help. I will keep some cotton too, but not too much, because cotton needs more watching and more hand work, and the young people in my house are often away working. I have farmed this land many years, and I know if I spread myself too thin, I lose on all sides.

For wheat, I will not save on fertilizer too much because if wheat turns yellow in spring, the loss is hard to make back. I will put base fertilizer before sowing, then give another round at jointing if the stand looks weak. Maize I plant right after wheat comes off, fast, with simple tillage because there is no time to wait. Cotton I keep on a smaller piece because it brings cash, but it takes labor for field care and picking. Water from the well costs money, so I will irrigate when the crop really needs it, not just because the calendar says so.
